name: Novobiocin

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in United States, first in 2009 — for liver harm, blood problems and serious skin reactions

examples.title: Patients Response to Early Switch To Oral:Osteomyelitis Study
examples.why: Not enough patient enrollment and lack of staffing

summary: Novobiocin was taken off the market in the United States starting in 2009 due to harm to the liver, blood, and skin [3]. In tests run on a small computer model rather than on people, the drug showed a high score of 81 for liver concern and a low score of 30 for heart concern [M]. A clinical study looking at switching patients to the oral drug was stopped early because of low patient enrollment and staffing shortages [5].
